title: A response-class rule fitted 38 earlier forward tests but predicted 2 of 6 new pre-registered US tests (fire, pollen, ticks); most later error came from level shifts that climate terms missed
abstract: Question: does response class (abiotic, timing, population, disease) predict which climate-response relations keep forecast skill in later years? Approach: we wrote and timestamped a plan before new outcomes. We coded 38 forward tests from 34 campaign publications and ran six new frozen tests: western US MTBS burned area against March-August temperature (train 1984-2005, test 2006-2024), CDC/NAB pollen onset and seasonal totals for trees and weeds at 38-48 US sites (train 2003-2013, test 2014-2024), and New York nymphal tick density in 26 counties (train 2008-2016, test 2017-2025). Results: in the earlier tests, abiotic and timing responses had a clear gain in 10 of 17 tests and other classes in 3 of 21 (Fisher p = 0.006). The class rule predicted only 2 of 6 new tests. Fire area had skill 0.42 (95% block interval 0.24 to 0.55) against the training mean. Pollen onset had no clear gain, while tree pollen totals (0.024) and tick density (0.055) had small clear gains. In all six tests a trailing mean beat the training mean by 11-55%. The frozen climate terms predicted at most 43% of the later level shifts; skill tracked the training-period signal fraction. A frozen slope with an updated level gave 0.445 for fire. In 23 tests with level information, frozen relations captured the later level in only 4. Limitations: unblinded coding by one coder, hypothesis-generating synthesis, observed rather than forecast weather, noisy pollen and tick monitoring, and post-plan exploratory analyses.

(b) New pre-registered tests: MSE skill of the frozen climate model against the training mean with 95% three-year block intervals, and whether the class rule predicted the outcome.

(a) Error of four forecasts in each new test, split into unit level error and year-to-year error, relative to the training-mean error. (b) Forward skill against training-period within-unit R2 of the selected climate term; open symbols are exploratory pollen checks.
